PullRequest.Title: sessions: rotate friendly personalized empty Inbox messages
PullRequest.Body:

Adds three friendly, rotating messages when the Inbox's **Ready for you** tab is empty.

- Reuses the welcome-message name: the configured override, otherwise the signed-in GitHub profile's first name. Messages also work without a name.
- Rotates between visits without changing the phrase on passive updates. Remembers the rotation position across reloads.
- Says "Your agents are working" only when a session is actually in the Working tab.
- Preserves filtered-result messages and other tabs' existing empty copy.
- Presents the same empty message in Accessible View.

Fixes #345920.

### Validation

- `corepack pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/test/browser/inboxNotificationsView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/test/browser/inboxNotificationsAccessibility.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts --reporter dot` — 331 tests passed.
- `corepack pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `corepack pnpm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Targeted ESLint on all eight changed TypeScript files and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Empty Inbox component fixtures in dark and light themes — rendered without errors and visually inspected.

### Manual testing

1. Open Inbox with no Ready for you rows; confirm a friendly message appears.
2. Set the existing welcome name and confirm Inbox uses the same name as new-session welcome phrases.
3. Leave and return to Inbox to cycle through the messages. Passive updates should not change the phrase.
4. With a Working session, the first phrase should mention working agents. With none, it should offer breathing room instead.
5. Search for a nonmatching term and confirm the existing filtered-result message remains.
6. Open Accessible View and confirm it includes the displayed empty-state message.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore the Inbox with an empty Ready for you tab and no configured welcome name
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The view constructor/render synchronously reads and advances the message index and renders an unnamed empty message. Default-account resolution, authentication-session lookup, and the GitHub /user request run asynchronously and are not awaited by canvas opening or rendering; only the later personalized text update depends on them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the profile-scoped rotation index from storage and enqueue the incremented value for delayed storage flush.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read and one coalescible write when the view presentation is first constructed; storage flush is delayed and grouped by the storage service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening or restoring Inbox did not read or write this rotation key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The in-memory read/write is synchronous but bounded; the backing database update is delayed and off the canvas render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the selected authentication session with authenticationService.getSessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one lookup for a cold provider/session key; concurrent Inbox and new-chat consumers coalesce through the module-level promise cache. No lookup occurs with a configured name or a warm cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inbox did not resolve a profile name; the new-chat welcome surface already performed this lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by Inbox render; the empty state is usable before completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the signed-in user's profile from the public or enterprise GitHub /user endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for each cold provider/session key across both Inbox and new-chat surfaces; successful, empty, and failed results are all promise-cached for the module lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inbox issued no profile request, while new chat already issued the same request and cache sharing can eliminate the Inbox request when that key is warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the canvas-open critical path; completion only replaces the already-rendered unnamed message with a personalized one.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One profile operation per distinct provider/session cache key, independent of Inbox row count; the empty-state render performs one additional short-circuit scan over all session rows to detect a Working row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The global Map stores the in-flight Promise, so concurrent WelcomeName instances for the same provider/session produce one authentication lookup/request. Distinct account keys are not limited, but account switching is user-paced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configured names and hidden surfaces bypass lookup. The first cold account key performs one lookup/request; the Promise, including undefined/failure results, is retained and reused across Inbox and new-chat instances. Account changes use a distinct provider/session key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor visibility, autorun, promise insertion before await, and the non-awaited refresh call establish the scheduling and coalescing behavior directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual network latency and Inbox row counts vary, but neither delays first render. The retained cache grows only with distinct signed-in session IDs, which is realistically small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds a single cold, off-critical-path profile request to support personalization, coalesces it with the pre-existing new-chat lookup, and adds only one O(rows) short-circuit scan when the Ready tab is empty.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hide and revisit an existing Inbox canvas
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setVisible(true) synchronously reloads the rotation index, enqueues the next value, then marks the retained canvas visible and reruns the list autorun. No profile boundary is repeated for an unchanged warm account key.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and advance the profile-scoped empty-message rotation index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read and one delayed/coalescible write per hidden-to-visible visit, regardless of tab contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Revisiting Inbox did not access a rotation key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only bounded in-memory storage operations occur before visibility changes; persistent database work is deferred by the storage flush delayer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with user-paced Inbox visits, not notifications or frames. Rendering still scales linearly with the rows already processed by the existing list autorun.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Visibility transitions are serialized on the UI thread; storage writes to the same key collapse in the storage pending-insert map before flush.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The welcome-name promise remains warm across retained visits; no repeated authentication or network request occurs for the same account key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed setVisible branch and storage implementation directly establish frequency and deferred persistence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visit frequency varies, but operations are one key read/write per visit and backing persistence is coalesced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new work is bounded, user-paced, and coalesced rather than frame- or row-scaled.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display a populated Inbox while the asynchronously fetched welcome name resolves or the configured name changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The WelcomeName observable is now a dependency of the visible list autorun, so a name change performs one additional full row filter and renderList pass even though populated or non-Ready tabs do not consume the name. There are no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls inside that rerender.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One extra O(number of session rows) list pass per profile resolution or relevant configuration change; profile resolution occurs once per cold account key and configuration changes are user-paced. Existing rendering already scales over the same row collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable reactions execute synchronously and serially; no concurrent render burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The profile cache bounds automatic name resolution to once per provider/session key. Warm keys can resolve immediately during construction, avoiding a later response-driven rerender.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the extra rerender path; lower for material user-visible cost because it occurs once and existing card rendering reuses cached card renderings.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inbox populations can vary, but the added pass is a single low-frequency event rather than repeated per row update, input event, or frame.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the dependency is broader than the empty Ready state, its effective multiplicity is one bounded pass per cold profile result and does not establish a realistic latency or throughput regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the new-session welcome surface after extracting profile-name resolution into WelcomeName
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rendering creates WelcomeName and starts the same conditional asynchronous profile resolution used before the PR. Welcome phrase rendering does not await account, authentication, or network completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve authentication sessions for the current GitHub provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold provider/session key, coalesced with Inbox consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: newChatWidget performed the same authentication lookup before extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial widget render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold provider/session key; shared cache can reduce total calls when Inbox already fetched it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: newChatWidget performed the same request with the same provider/session-keyed promise cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial widget render critical path; only personalization waits.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup per distinct signed-in provider/session key, independent of widget content or session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: In-flight requests for the same key are coalesced globally; separate keys can overlap only after account changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cache semantics are preserved and broadened across both surfaces; configured names and disabled welcome phrases bypass the request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the deleted implementation and equivalent added WelcomeName implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for causality; the call path and count are equivalent or improved through cross-surface reuse.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression and no qualifying regression-fix record. This is a behavior-preserving extraction for new chat with potentially better cross-surface coalescing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Accessible View for Inbox content
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessible View first reads the already-rendered empty-state text. When absent, it follows the existing row mapping and preview lookup path; no new external boundary is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Empty content is O(1); populated fallback remains O(number of session rows), as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous content generation with no queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses already-rendered DOM text and existing preview map; no profile fetch is initiated by Accessible View itself.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the nullish short-circuit in the changed provider callback.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The empty-state branch avoids rather than adds collection mapping, while the populated path is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all eight changed files and traced Inbox construction, visibility, rendering, storage persistence, profile cache ownership, authentication/network lookup, new-chat reuse, and Accessible View. The only new expensive boundary is one coalesced, off-critical-path cold GitHub profile lookup for Inbox plus a delayed one-key storage write per visit; neither establishes a material performance regression. No findings or regression-fix records were submitted.
